api.note: API v1 alone does not establish review-v2 or private Web auth-status capability.

features.note: All three features are additive on review-v2 only. dense-128 raises the finding page from 32 to 128 and stays bounded by the 64 KiB body ceiling Core 0.10.0 serves, and reason-v1 adds a reason to each not_evaluated finding. A request without the header answers the published 32-finding, seven-key document; a header on review-v1, an unknown or repeated token, or an empty part is invalid_request, and a response that enabled a feature echoes the accepted set in the same header. ambiguous-mention-v1 (Core 0.14.0) requires reason-v1 and reports a one-character resonator name the matcher could not settle, whose source text meets the evidence threshold, as a not_evaluated finding with reason ambiguous_mention. clients_request is the pair Web 0.5.0 and Windows 0.7.0 send on every review-v2 request; they add ambiguous-mention-v1 only when GET /v1/capabilities lists it.

manuscript.note: v1 and v2 keep their meaning, and an imported v1 or v2 report, a document-mode choice or a semantic decision stays history, not a fresh check. v3 adds per-segment term results for long manuscripts: a saved segment result is reused only when its content hashes, review basis and request inputs all match a live review-v2 basis. v4 keeps v3's 13 top-level keys, the 44 MiB file limit and the canonical bytes, and raises the findings, resolutions and choices limits from 32 to 128 while allowing a reason on a not_evaluated finding; only the label v4 brings those limits, so a v1, v2 or v3 file keeps its 32-item caps and rejects reason. A writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4, then v5). v5 adds a review_features list, the ambiguous_mention reason and segmentation-v1-gaps segment records and otherwise keeps v4; it ships in Web 0.5.0 and Windows 0.7.0, and Web 0.4.5 and earlier and Windows 0.6.6 and earlier reject a v5 file. The v4 contract ships in Web 0.4.0, 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 and in Windows 0.6.0, 0.6.1 and 0.6.2, not in Web 0.3.1 or Windows 0.5.1, which reject a v4 file; the shipped-release records below keep the format each release was recorded with.

previous_release.note: v0.13.0 is a translation-direction, prose-preservation and terms release on top of v0.12.0 (#314, #316, #317, #318, #319, #320, #322, #324). Automatic direction (#319): without forced_to_chinese the direction is read from the normalized user text, and text with CJK characters translates to Chinese only when its Latin letters outnumber its CJK characters more than four to one (v0.12.0 translated to English whenever any CJK character was present). Prose preservation (#318, #322): Core keeps the user's text verbatim apart from Unicode NFKC, line endings and whitespace, SentenceTranslator.prepare_text no longer deletes spoiler tags, version tags or quote bars, wrapper cleanup moves to wuwaterm.normalize.strip_telegram_wrapper_noise (called by the Telegram adapters), and channel_post_handler strips the markers once for every plain stage. wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v10 (MATCHER_REVISION 57428b88978597d95840f56ba0080a4f8fb11d4860fe8ea5532d3c1e7c6a918a) turns the single-character mention judgment into classify_single_character_mention without changing which mentions are admitted, so manuscript-v3 and v4 results saved under wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v9 become stale after the upgrade and are re-reviewed. Stdlib-only wuwaterm.structural_checks is extracted and the inspect.signature compatibility bridges in sentence.py are removed (#319, #320). MY-229 eval_semantic hardening (#316), ADR 0021 with the H3 / raw-baseline evaluation protocol (#317) and the offline Rust text-kernel and Aho-Corasick study (#314) add no runtime path. Dictionary builder logic, SQLite schema 2, data pin 9218d612 (3.7.0 / 3.7.8 / 8975829), terms.db contents, every wuwaterm_api route, OpenAPI/HTTP contracts (except info.version 0.13.0), the en->zh omit default and the zh->en disabled default are unchanged from v0.12.0, so v0.12.0 hosts can upgrade with --runtime-only. A library consumer that relied on Core to delete wrapper noise, such as the standalone Telegram product, must now call strip_telegram_wrapper_noise itself. On source_commit e5b7f1a8, ci.yml main push run 45673369149, CodeQL run 45673367695, Dependency audit run 45673368136, release.yml dry run 45673459244, release.yml (dry_run=false) run 45676030113 and promote-images run 45677072410 all succeeded. All four published assets (wuwaterm-0.13.0-py3-none-any.whl 542,034 bytes, wuwaterm-0.13.0.tar.gz 527,617 bytes, release-manifest.json 861 bytes, SHA256SUMS 188 bytes) were downloaded and verified via sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.
